record.paper_title: Cooperative Games with Incomplete Information: Some Open Problems
record.context_brief: Coco value for more than two players
record.original_question: How can the cooperative-competitive (coco) solution for Bayesian games with transferable utility be extended from the two-player case to settings with more than two players?

evidence.quote: A. Kalai and E. Kalai (2011) point out the following open problems: extension of the coco value in the TU case for more than two players and in the NTU case for two players or more, and construction of a second best analog of the coco value for environments that do not satisfy ex post observability conditions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. A Bayesian game with transferable utility (TU) consists of: a finite set of players $N=\{1,\dots,n\}$; for each player $i$ a finite set of types $T_i$ and a finite set of actions $A_i$; a common prior probability distribution $p$ on the type profile space $T=\prod_i T_i$; and, for each player $i$, a payoff function $u_i:A\times T\to\mathbb{R}$ where $A=\prod_i A_i$. Utility is freely transferable across players (side payments are allowed) and players can sign binding contracts contingent on observed types and actions.

For two-player Bayesian TU games (the case $n=2$), Kalai and Kalai defined the cooperative-competitive (coco) value, which uniquely satisfies a list of natural axioms (including Pareto efficiency, shift invariance, monotonicity in actions, payoff dominance, and a relevant invariance/symmetry property), and which decomposes each game into a purely cooperative team game plus a purely competitive zero-sum game.

Problem. Extend the coco value from two-player Bayesian TU games to Bayesian TU games with $n\ge 3$ players. Specifically, define a solution concept assigning a payoff vector in $\mathbb{R}^n$ (as a function of the game data $(N,(T_i),(A_i),p,(u_i))$) that:
(i) reduces to the coco value in the two-player case;
(ii) satisfies natural generalizations of the axioms characterizing the two-player coco value (such as efficiency, individual rationality with respect to suitable threat values, symmetry, additivity, and a dummy/null-player property);
(iii) admits a decomposition of the game into cooperative and competitive components consistent with the two-player construction.

Either exhibit such an extension and prove that it is well defined and uniquely characterized, or prove an impossibility result identifying the precise axiomatic obstruction to such an extension for $n\ge 3$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been actively studied. A subsequent work titled "On the difficulty of extending the coco value to games with more than two players" shows that adding a mild dummy-player axiom to the original coco axioms produces an inconsistent system once $n\ge 3$, indicating an impossibility-type obstruction. Other authors (e.g., in cooperative strategic games literature) have proposed alternative axiomatic extensions to $n$-player Bayesian TU games using efficiency, balanced threats, symmetry, null player, and additivity. So while partial extensions exist under modified axioms, a fully canonical extension preserving all the original two-player coco axioms is provably impossible. The problem is best described as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On the difficulty of extending the coco value to games with more than two players
status_evidence.snippet: Adding a mild dummy player axiom to the list of axioms for the coco value makes the axioms inconsistent when there are more than two players.
status_evidence.claim: An impossibility result shows that natural axiomatic extensions of the coco value fail for n>=3.

status_evidence.title: Cooperative strategic games (Theoretical Economics)
status_evidence.snippet: Axioms of efficiency, balanced threats, symmetry, null player, and additivity imply a unique value solution for n-player Bayesian games.
status_evidence.claim: Alternative n-player extensions for Bayesian TU games exist under modified axiom sets.
